brief.title: Tea at the Ninth Stall
brief.premise: A hedge-witch tea merchant follows a travelling fair that appears only in leap-season, trying to win back her family's lost stall before the fair folds its lanes and moves on.
constraints: Conflicts are settled by bargains, contests and trade, never violence.

world.name: The Thistledown Fair
world.description: A travelling fair that unfolds its lanes only in leap-season, where stall rights are held in favours, debts are settled in trade, and the fair itself seems to remember every promise made under its lanterns.

locations.name: Leap Lane
locations.description: The fair's main way, which appears in an ordinary field at leap-season and folds away at season's end.

locations.name: The Ninth Stall
locations.description: A shuttered stall at the lane's turn whose lease was forfeited on an unkept favour a generation ago.

locations.name: The Kettle Commons
locations.description: The cluster of tea tents where merchants trade gossip, samples and favours.

locations.name: The Wishing Barn
locations.description: The tallykeepers' barn where every promised favour is written on a wishing tag and hung until kept.

factions.name: The Stallholders' Round
factions.description: The merchants who hold the fair's leases and vote the stall rights.

factions.name: The Tallykeepers
factions.description: The clerks who record every favour on wishing tags and judge disputes of debt.

factions.name: The Carter Kin
factions.description: The families whose wains carry the fair between fields and keep the lanes' secrets.

rules.statement: The fair exists only in leap-season; at season's end the lanes fold back into ordinary fields.
Debts at the fair are paid in favours, and a favour once promised must be kept before the fair moves.
No contest at the fair may risk harm; disputes go to the Tallykeepers and are settled by bargain or contest.
The Ninth Stall's lease can be claimed only by the family that lost it, before the third bell of closing day.

history.name: The First Fair
history.description: The fair appeared uninvited in a fallow field, traded for a season, and left a lane where none had been.

history.name: The Forfeit of the Ninth
history.description: A tea merchant's family lost their stall when a promised favour went unkept past the third bell.

history.name: The Tally Accord
history.description: The tallykeepers were given authority over favour-debts after a season of duelling claims.

conflicts.name: The Ninth Claim
conflicts.description: The Carter Kin are quietly selling the Ninth Stall's lease, while the family that forfeited it still holds a claim.

conflicts.name: The Favour Shortage
conflicts.description: More favours are owed than can be kept before closing day, and the tallykeepers must rule which debts ride with the fair.

evidence_summary: The world, cast and storyboard satisfy the brief's gentle travelling-fair setting; deterministic validators are clean and there are no blocking defects.
